public_payload.normalized_proposition: If Grok is offered to every X Premium+ subscriber at $16/month, it will not be profitable.
conditions: if Grok is offered to every Premium+ subscriber

statement.excerpt: Musk is already using Grok as a marketing vehicle for X Premium+’s $16-a-month subscription, and if he actually offers it to every subscriber, there’s no way in hell that this is a profitable transaction.

from_speaker: if he actually offers it to every subscriber
there’s no way in hell that this is a profitable transaction
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that including Grok in the $16 monthly Premium+ offering produces no positive profit after attributable costs.
The surrounding analyst-cost estimates imply an estimated economic calculation, not a stated GAAP or net-income measure.
Every subscriber means availability across the subscription tier, not that every subscriber actually uses Grok.
The $16 price refers to the US monthly offering; local prices and annual plans require separate treatment.
No deadline or minimum operating period is stated.
criteria.support_condition: After tier-wide availability, comparable revenue and attributable costs show the $16 offering was unprofitable across the relevant operating period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable product-level accounts show a positive profit for the offering while Grok was included at $16 per month.
